definition: A method that controls which areas are shown or hidden without erasing the original.
example: I adjust how much of the image is visible with a mask.

definition: The outer line of an element. In print file work, it can also mean converting text from editable characters into shape outlines.
example: In the print copy, I outline the text.

definition: The role that manages a project's scope, schedule, cost, and progress, along with collaboration among stakeholders.
example: The project manager coordinates the predecessor tasks and the schedule.

definition: The role that analyzes data to explain phenomena and produce the evidence needed for business decisions.
example: The data analyst checks the drop-off points.

definition: The role that analyzes data to explain phenomena and produce the evidence needed for business decisions.
example: I analyze return and repurchase rates by size together with the data analyst.

definition: The activity of inspecting and managing whether products and the production process meet set quality standards.
example: In print QC, I check the trim position and color bleeding.
note: This is the quality-management context when producing design deliverables such as packaging, printed matter, and physical products.

definition: A method of manufacturing and supplying products to match the ordering company's requirements and brand.
example: I hand the designed goods to the OEM vendor and align the drawings and finish samples.
note: This is the context of commissioning an external manufacturer to produce designed physical products and goods.

definition: A method in which the manufacturer handles both product development and design and production, supplying it under the ordering company's brand.
example: I discuss the exterior design and color to match the ODM vendor's product structure.
note: This is the context of developing and manufacturing physical products together with an external manufacturer.

definition: An abbreviation meaning "for your information."
example: FYI: I recorded the related decision in the document.

definition: A term for the state in which an ad or broadcast is actually being transmitted or placed.
example: After delivering the final master, I check the picture and sound of the on-air video.

definition: A term for ending transmission of an ad or broadcast, or the state of not being transmitted.
example: I check the schedule for swapping the broadcast creative in time for the off-air date.

definition: Delivering material in advance while requesting or agreeing that it not be reported or made public before a set time.
example: Please distribute the new-product material after confirming the embargo time.
note: This is the press-release timing context. Distinguish it from the economic and trade meaning of an import-export ban. The date, time zone, and scope must be communicated clearly.

definition: An advertising method that places a product or brand within a broadcast or video content to expose it.
example: I review a PPL arrangement where the product appears in line with the scene flow.
note: This entry is product placement. It is not merged with the meaning of pay per lead.

definition: A method of segmenting customers and analyzing their characteristics based on recency, frequency, and monetary value of purchases.
example: I use RFM to find the customer segment whose recent purchases have declined.
note: In purchase analysis, it uses recency, frequency, and monetary value. Distinguish it from simple visit metrics and define the analysis criteria.

definition: A contract model in which an agreed scope of work is carried out continuously over a period for a regular fee.
example: I separate the work included in the monthly retainer from additional production.

definition: The process of revisiting content after a briefing or activity and organizing the interpretation, results, and follow-up actions. In advertising, it is also used when a team re-organizes a received brief.
example: After the client meeting, I gather the questions to confirm in the debrief.

definition: The central idea that ties a campaign's message and expression into one direction.
example: I check whether this concept is conveyed consistently in the video and in stores.

definition: The actions and experiences a customer goes through as they recognize a need and move through exploration, purchase, use, and repurchase.
example: In the customer journey, I find the friction just before purchase.

definition: The degree to which consumers can recognize or recall a brand.
example: Brand awareness is compared by aligning the survey method and question conditions.

definition: The brand consumers recall first when given a product category, or the proportion that does so.
example: I survey the top-of-mind awareness in the beverage category.

definition: The value that awareness, associations, trust, loyalty, and more about a brand add to a product or business.
example: I also review the impact a discount campaign will have on brand equity.

definition: A go-to-market execution strategy that defines to whom and with what value, price, channel, and sales method a product will be offered.
example: In the GTM, I first decide the initial customers and sales channels.

definition: A collaboration method in which two or more brands use their names and assets together to create a product or campaign.
example: In co-branding, I set the rules for using the two brands' logos.

definition: A metric that divides ad spend by the measured number of app installs, or a pricing model based on installs.
example: I look at CPI together with the actual usage rate after installation.

definition: A metric that divides the cost spent on acquiring customers over a defined period and scope by the number of newly acquired customers.
example: Before comparing CAC, I align which sales and marketing costs to include.

definition: A small image or tracking code placed on a web page or message to measure actions such as visits, views, and conversions.
example: I check that the checkout-complete event is not double-counted by the pixel.
note: This is the ad-measurement context. Distinguish it from the pixel that makes up an image.

definition: The ratio of engagement counts such as likes, comments, shares, and saves against a chosen base such as reach, impressions, or followers.
example: When comparing engagement rate, I check whether the denominator is reach or followers.
note: Because the denominator and the scope of engagement actions differ by platform and report, verify that the formula is the same.

definition: Content such as reviews, photos, videos, and posts created by users themselves.
example: I use UGC with permission in the campaign.

definition: A content format that delivers the key content or scenes in a short length. The exact length criterion varies by platform and context.
example: I restructure the key content of the interview into short-form.

definition: A customer with no qualifying activity, such as a purchase or use, over a defined period.
example: I set the dormant-customer criterion as the most recent purchase date.

definition: The opinions and requests customers convey, such as inquiries, complaints, suggestions, and reviews.
example: I group recurring VOC and define improvement tasks.

definition: A metric from a recommendation-intent survey that subtracts the proportion of detractors from the proportion of promoters.
example: I analyze the NPS figure together with the reasons for not recommending.
note: In a typical 0-10 survey, 9-10 are promoters and 0-6 are detractors. It is not the same metric as satisfaction itself.

definition: Communication activity that, in a crisis such as controversy or an incident, coordinates fact-checking, the message, the audience, and the timing of announcements.
example: In crisis communication, I separate confirmed facts from unconfirmed information.

definition: A contract that sets the scope and obligations for keeping shared information confidential.
example: Before delivering the material, I check the information covered by the NDA.

definition: The work of reflecting review feedback or changes, or the resulting version.
example: Please mark the changed items in this revision separately.

definition: A procedure in which the person in charge confirms the result or conditions and approves moving to the next stage.
example: I proceed with production based on the signed-off file.

definition: An activity of freely proposing and developing many ideas to broaden the direction of a solution.
example: In brainstorming, we first gather a variety of ideas.

definition: Recording work methods, structure, decisions, and usage so that others can understand and build on them.
example: Please document the reason for the change along with how to use it.

definition: A metric that views net profit as a ratio of the cost invested. It is calculated by aligning the scope and period of cost and profit.
example: To compare ROI, you first need to check which costs are included.

definition: Progressively accumulating the evidence, context, and preparation needed to reach a conclusion or result.
example: Please build up logically from the proposal's background to the solution.

definition: A term for a situation of exchanging questions, opinions, or work back and forth. It is also used when responsibility or requests are repeatedly passed along.
example: To reduce the ping-pong, I decide with the owner which items to settle.

definition: An informal expression for a proposal or deliverable being rejected or criticized.
example: The draft got shot down, so I first organized the reasons for the objection.
note: This is an informal expression. In official documents, it is clearer to describe the actual situation specifically, such as a rejection, refusal, or revision request.

definition: A development method that repeats a cycle of first writing a test for a small feature, then writing code that passes it, and then improving the structure.
example: With TDD, I test boundary conditions first and then proceed with the implementation.

definition: A structure that divides an application into relatively independently developable and deployable services connected by communication.
example: Before splitting into MSA, I define the data ownership and service boundaries.

definition: A structure that composes multiple features into a single application deployment unit.
example: We start as a monolith early on and manage it by splitting the internal modules.
note: It means a single deployment unit; it does not necessarily mean the structure is bad or lacks internal module separation.

definition: A name-and-value setting passed in from the environment in which a program runs. It is used for various settings such as paths, run modes, and connection information.
example: I use environment variables to separate the test and production connection addresses.
note: .env is one file format used to define environment variables. An environment variable does not mean only secret information, nor does it automatically encrypt its value.

definition: Marking a feature or API as no longer recommended for use. It may keep working for compatibility.
example: In the deprecation notice, I check the replacement API and the migration method.
note: Being deprecated differs from being already removed and non-functional. Check the provider's guidance for the removal schedule.

definition: A development method that proceeds sequentially through stages such as requirements, design, implementation, and verification.
example: In a waterfall project, I define the approval criteria for each stage.

definition: A development process that connects integrating and verifying changes with delivering and deploying software. CD means continuous delivery or continuous deployment.
example: In CI/CD, I stop the pipeline from proceeding to the next stage when a test fails.
note: Continuous delivery is an approach that keeps the software in a deployable state, while continuous deployment is an approach that automates even reflecting verified changes into production.

definition: The time during which a service or system cannot be used.
example: I announce the downtime needed for maintenance in advance.

definition: The flow and volume of data and requests going to and from a network or service. Depending on measurement, it means transfer volume or request count.
example: I distinguish whether a traffic increase is in request count or transfer volume.

definition: The delay until a result appears in a specific segment of a request, processing, or communication.
example: I check the latency of slow requests, not just the average.

definition: A model of receiving and using computing, storage, and other resources on demand over a network.
example: In the cloud, I manage the required resources and their usage.

definition: Software that connects systems or components, or performs common functions in the middle of the request-processing flow.
example: In the authentication middleware, I check the request's permissions.

definition: A development method in which two people look at the same work together and collaborate on implementation and review.
example: I handle complex changes with pair programming.

definition: A collaborative event in which teams refine ideas and build a working deliverable within a set period.
example: In a hackathon, I decide the scope that will demonstrate the core hypothesis.

definition: A metaphor for code whose control flow or dependencies are so tangled that it is hard to understand and modify.
example: I organize the spaghetti code by splitting it into small units of responsibility.
note: "Crap code" is slang that disparages code quality. In code review, it is better to explain the structural and maintainability problems specifically.

definition: Blocking the immediate problem with a limited fix before resolving the root cause.
example: After recovering with a patch-up fix, I also plan a root-cause fix.

definition: An action that affects the outside of a function, such as changing external state, writing files, or I/O, beyond the return value. In the field, it also refers to the unexpected impact of a change.
example: I separate out this function's side effects to make it easier to test.
note: A side effect is not necessarily a bug. Distinguish external state changes from unexpected regression errors.

definition: A vulnerability or attack in which input values are misinterpreted as part of a query, allowing unintended database commands to run.
example: I check whether SQL injection prevention is applied in the user-input handling.

definition: The situation and flow in which a user or external actor interacts with a system to achieve a goal.
example: I organize the exception conditions of the order-cancellation use case.

definition: An individual function or characteristic a product or software provides.
example: I define the scope of the features to include in this release.

definition: A document that explains screen composition, navigation, behavior, data, exception conditions, and more to set the implementation baseline.
example: Please include the empty state and error state in the screen specification too.
note: This is the SB in the service-planning context. Its purpose and composition differ from a scene-by-scene storyboard for video.

definition: An admin system where operators handle internal service tasks such as members, orders, and content.
example: In the back office, I check the order change history.

definition: An interface for operating a system through visual elements such as windows, icons, menus, and buttons.
example: I connect the GUI's save button to the actual file-save action.

definition: An interface for operating a system through visual elements such as windows, icons, menus, and buttons.
example: In the GUI, I arrange frequently used functions so they are easy to find.

definition: An interaction designed for a small unit of user action and system response, such as a state change or feedback.
example: I implement the loading-complete microinteraction so it also works with reduced-motion settings.

definition: An interaction designed for a small unit of user action and system response, such as a state change or feedback.
example: I signal that the save state has changed with a microinteraction.

definition: Changing the core hypothesis and direction of a product, customer, or revenue model based on what has been learned.
example: Based on the validation results, I review a pivot that changes the customer segment.

definition: A unit indicating the number of dots an output device and the like render over a length of one inch.
example: I check the output device's DPI and the image's PPI separately.
note: It is a different concept from PPI, the pixel density of an image. The value needed varies by output method, size, viewing distance, and more.

definition: A structure that designs the shape, folds, locking, and assembly method of paper packaging.
example: With a carton-structure sample, I check how the product is held and how it opens.
note: This is the structural design of packaging. The cut lines that mark the cutting and folding positions are drawing elements that convey that structure to production.

definition: A short text attached to a photo or illustration to explain its content, situation, or information.
example: Please briefly note the place and shooting situation in the caption.

definition: The work of digitally creating the form and structure of an object in three-dimensional space.
example: In the modeling stage, I first get the product's proportions right.

definition: The polygonal faces that make up the surface of a 3D model.
example: I adjust the polygon layout to refine the shape of the curved surface.

definition: The work of applying color, pattern, and detail to a model's surface to compose the appearance of its material.
example: In texturing, I match the scale of the fabric pattern.

definition: A method of designing drawings or the form and dimensions of products and spaces with computer tools.
example: In the CAD drawing, I check the dimensions between parts.

definition: A field that studies and designs products, environments, and tasks to suit human physical and cognitive characteristics.
example: From an ergonomics standpoint, I review the handle size and the effort it takes to operate.

definition: A compositional principle of shooting from one side of an imaginary axis connecting people or actions to keep the left-right relationship and gaze direction on screen consistent.
example: In a dialogue scene, I set the camera positions based on the 180-degree rule.
note: It is a compositional principle for conveying spatial relationships. Deliberately crossing the axis is also possible, and it is not an absolute prohibition.

definition: A shot that presents a scene's location, spatial relationship, and situation so the audience understands it.
example: Before the indoor dialogue, I show the building's exterior as an establishing shot.

definition: A shot that shows a person's expression or movement as they react to a line or event.
example: I cut in a reaction shot of the person who heard the explanation.

definition: A shot that turns the viewpoint toward the other party or the opposite subject that was being looked at in the preceding shot. It is used to alternate between two people in a dialogue scene.
example: In the reverse shot too, I keep the two people's gaze directions consistent.
note: It does not mean the camera is necessarily turned exactly 180 degrees. Consider the person's gaze and the spatial relationship.

definition: A filter that reduces the amount of light entering the lens so you can use a desired aperture or shutter setting even in bright conditions.
example: Outdoors, I use an ND filter to open up the aperture.

definition: A table that organizes the running order and timing of a broadcast or event, along with cues for video, audio, and talent.
example: In the cue sheet, I check the next video and the mic-switch timing.
note: It is a table centered on running cues. Distinguish it from a call sheet, which organizes the staff assembly, location, and shooting schedule.

definition: The staff or department that sets up and operates camera-support and movement equipment and shooting support rigs. Depending on the country and set, they also handle light-shaping equipment.
example: I check the camera movement path and equipment setup with the grip team.

definition: A person who stands in the designated position in place of an actor while lighting, composition, and focus are being prepared.
example: Before the actor's rehearsal, I check the light and composition with a stand-in.
note: It is a role that helps with setup. Distinguish it from a double, who performs actual acting, dangerous actions, or stands in for a body part on camera.

definition: The main footage that delivers the central story content, such as interviews or key actions. It is composed together with B-roll, the supplementary footage.
example: I first build the story with A-roll and supplement it with B-roll.

definition: The work of creating a screen's visual effects using live-action footage, digital imagery, compositing, and more.
example: Before shooting, I check the elements needed for VFX compositing.

definition: A term for a shot scene or a particular person's footage being removed wholesale during editing.
example: The redundant explanation section was cut entirely for the sake of flow.

definition: A voice heard over a scene while the speaker is not shown on screen. It is used for narration, monologue, and more.
example: I lay the protagonist's VO over the scene to convey their thoughts.

definition: A term for a take that failed to achieve the intended result due to problems such as acting, sound, or focus, or that state.
example: A focus problem caused an NG, so we shoot it once more.

definition: The shooting footage and arrangement of various compositions, sizes, and reactions secured so a scene can be edited.
example: For the dialogue scene, I secure coverage of the whole and both reactions.

definition: A value that expresses the color character of light in kelvin. It is used to compare the light source and camera settings when judging color balance.
example: I check the color-temperature difference between the window light and the indoor lighting.

definition: A setting that corrects the color influence of the light source so white and other colors are recorded to the intended reference.
example: When the location changes, I check the white balance again.

definition: A term for the short time around sunrise and sunset that is good for using the light and sky color. Conditions and duration vary by location, season, and weather.
example: I prepare the magic-hour scenes to match the on-site daylight conditions.
note: Golden hour and magic hour are sometimes used interchangeably, but the range they refer to varies by set. Do not assume a fixed 20-30 minutes.

definition: A compositional method of dividing the frame into three parts horizontally and vertically and placing key elements near the lines or their intersections.
example: I use the rule of thirds as a reference to balance the subject and background.

definition: A composition arranged so that the shape or placement corresponds left-right or top-bottom around an axis.
example: I emphasize the order of the space with the hallway's symmetrical composition.

definition: A composition that places the main subject in the center of the frame to draw the eye.
example: Please show the product neatly with a center composition.

definition: A tool that manages measurement and advertising tags and their firing conditions on websites and the like.
example: In Google Tag Manager, I verify that the purchase event fires only once.
note: It shares the abbreviation GTM with go-to-market strategy but has a different meaning. Initial setup and data-layer design may require development work.

definition: In GA4, the proportion of sessions that do not qualify as engaged sessions. The definition differs by analytics tool and version.
example: Before comparing bounce rate, I check GA4's engaged-session criterion.
note: Do not judge a GA4 bounce by a single-page visit alone. Also distinguish it from user and subscription churn.

definition: An attribute that segments data, such as traffic source, device, or region.
example: I compare purchase conversion by device dimension.

definition: A value that represents a measured quantity or ratio, such as view count, revenue, or conversion count.
example: Please align the aggregation basis of the dimensions and metrics.

definition: A visualization that represents the magnitude or distribution of values with color. In web analytics, it is used to examine distributions such as clicks and scrolling.
example: I use a heatmap to check the click distribution around the purchase button.

definition: The period during which conversions after a touchpoint, such as an ad click or view, are credited to that touchpoint's performance.
example: I do not directly compare conversion counts from reports with different attribution windows.

definition: A promise that organizes the distinctive value that becomes the reason a customer chooses this product or service.
example: I check whether the UVP connects to an actual customer problem.

definition: A brand that keeps a relationship with the parent brand while having a separate identity for a specific customer or product group.
example: I define the sub-brand's role and its relationship with the parent brand.

definition: A structure that organizes the relationships, hierarchy, and naming conventions among multiple brands and product groups.
example: I name the new line in line with the brand architecture.

definition: A customer's tendency to continuously prefer and choose a particular brand.
example: I survey the reasons for repurchase to examine brand loyalty.

definition: Activity that re-encourages use or purchase from customers who have churned or become less active.
example: Before sending win-back messages, I segment the reasons for churn.

definition: A metric indicating the total amount of goods and services transacted on a platform and the like over a defined period.
example: In the GMV report, I also note the basis for reflecting cancellations and returns.

definition: The average order value, calculated by dividing the revenue over a defined period by the number of orders.
example: When looking at AOV, I check the order count and the basis for reflecting returns.

definition: A distribution method in which the seller does not directly hold or ship inventory; when they pass on the order information, the supplier sends it to the customer.
example: In the dropshipping contract, I define who handles shipping and returns.

definition: A term, from a domestic seller's perspective, for a transaction in which an overseas consumer buys directly from a domestic online store.
example: I check the shipping country and return instructions for reverse-direct-purchase orders.

definition: A method of applying game elements such as points, missions, progress, and rewards to other activities.
example: I apply gamification to increase learning engagement.

definition: A method of granting a purchase opportunity and the like to applicants by random draw.
example: I announce the raffle entry period and the purchase deadline after winning.
note: This entry is the purchase-opportunity draw context. Do not merge the whole of a giveaway with a raffle or draw-based sale.

definition: A marketing method that pays compensation based on defined performance generated through an affiliate's referrals, links, and the like.
example: I align the performance-recognition conditions of affiliate marketing.

definition: A program that drives new customers' sign-ups and purchases through referrals from existing customers and the like.
example: I announce the participation conditions and benefits of the referral program.

definition: The sum of the ratings of individual ad exposures. Because it includes repeated exposure, it differs from net reach.
example: I check repeated exposure by looking at GRP and reach together.

definition: A media-efficiency metric that divides ad spend by the rating points secured.
example: I compare CPR using the same target and survey basis.

definition: The share a particular brand occupies in a defined market or medium against total ad spend, impressions, mentions, and the like.
example: I state that the SOV was calculated on an ad-spend basis.

definition: A method of handling the buying, selling, and execution of ad inventory through automated systems.
example: In programmatic advertising, I check the media quality and targeting conditions.
note: Real-time bidding (RTB) is one of the transaction methods, and not all programmatic transactions are open auctions.
